guidedTour.title: BrowserRT Kernel Kit guided tour
guidedTour.purpose: Make the Kernel Kit demo evaluable by a human: what to click, why it matters, which evidence should appear, what exact commands verify it, and which claims remain unearned.

tourSteps.label: Orient on the narrow wedge
tourSteps.action: Read the page lede and proof cards before clicking anything.
tourSteps.whyItMatters: The demo should look like a practical Kernel Kit wedge, not an unfenced browser OS claim.

tourSteps.label: Run the integrated success path
tourSteps.action: Click “Run Kernel Kit demo” or call window.BrowserRTKernelKitDemo.run().
tourSteps.whyItMatters: This shows one useful browser-local workflow through boot, Worker agent, object ref, admission, storage lane, and trace receipt.
tourSteps.nonClaimReminder: No throughput, latency, SLO, or real performance claim.

tourSteps.label: Reload and verify the OPFS handoff
tourSteps.action: Reload the page after a run, then click “Read stored handoff”.
tourSteps.whyItMatters: A human can exercise the same localStorage + OPFS readback path as the CDP proof without hidden arguments.
tourSteps.nonClaimReminder: No OPFS durability, fsync, quota, eviction, crash-recovery, browser-restart, or multi-tab coordination claim.

tourSteps.label: Export the last receipt
tourSteps.action: Click “Export last receipt” and inspect the BrowserRT JSON plus trace-shaped sketches.
tourSteps.whyItMatters: The demo creates portable evidence without claiming production observability or external trace compatibility.

tourSteps.label: Trigger a controlled bounded failure
tourSteps.action: Click “Run controlled failure” to prove missing-handoff failure reporting without provider mutation.
tourSteps.whyItMatters: A useful runtime substrate must explain bounded failures, not merely show happy paths.

tourSteps.label: Compare success and failure traces
tourSteps.action: Click “Compare success/failure traces” and inspect success-only/failure-only evidence.
tourSteps.whyItMatters: The workbench teaches what changed and what stayed bounded across the two paths.

tourSteps.label: Create the diagnostic runbook
tourSteps.action: Click “Create diagnostic runbook” and follow its exact commands before changing contracts.
tourSteps.whyItMatters: Future sessions need an office handoff that is specific enough to respect and cheap enough to run.

tourSteps.label: Build the support bundle
tourSteps.action: Click “Build support bundle” and keep the bundle with any bug report or future revision note.
tourSteps.whyItMatters: One portable object prevents future sessions from reconstructing state from many panels.

tourSteps.label: Respect the shelf
tourSteps.action: Before proposing the next step, read the non-claims and cloudtainer shelf boundaries.
tourSteps.whyItMatters: The demo is useful because it earns narrow claims and keeps unearned claims visible.

future-session-maintainer: Run browser proof only when browser budget is intentional
Update docs/non-claims before widening the demo
browser-heavy-app-builder: Decide whether this would remove app-specific runtime glue
runtime-library-author: Check provider/non-claim boundaries before adding primitives
skeptical-evaluator: Ask what user workflow this would shorten

acceptanceGates: A human can run the page without reading source first.
The browser proof drives the same page API a human uses.
The support bundle preserves success, reload, failure, comparison, runbook, exact commands, and non-claims.
The guided tour tells future sessions what to click, what evidence to expect, and what not to claim.
nextUsefulImprovements: Add support-bundle import/validate so a future session can paste a bundle and get the tour back.
Add a tiny screenshot/golden-page sanity check if cloudtainer browser budget allows.
Add one OPFS journal/manifest skeleton only after the demo remains legible.
Keep browser/CDP tests explicit by id/tier.
